getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.summary: Sign in, choose your language, find your way around the menus and sign out.

sections.heading: Sign in
paragraphs: Sign in with your AHDA username and password on the [[identityAccess.signIn.tabs.directory]] tab. The other sign-in options on that page are marked [[identityAccess.signIn.comingSoon]] and cannot be used yet.
The platform never resets passwords. If you have forgotten yours, contact the AHDA IT service desk.
sections.note: If you hold the System Administrator role, the platform also asks for the verification code from your authenticator app each time you sign in.

sections.heading: Choose your language
paragraphs: You can use the platform in Arabic or English. Your choice is remembered in this browser, and dates are shown in the Gregorian calendar with Latin digits in both languages, so they match what you type and what you see in exports.
steps: In the top bar, open [[common.language]].
Choose English or العربية.
The whole page switches at once, including its direction: Arabic reads right to left.

sections.heading: Find your way around
paragraphs: The [[common.menu.label]] on the side lists only the areas your roles can use, so two colleagues may see different menus. Choosing a menu opens its first screen and lists its other screens underneath.

[[common.shell.create]] in the top bar starts a new [[projects.nav.create]] or [[common.shell.createChangeRequest]] from anywhere. A number next to [[common.menu.requestsApprovals]] or [[common.menu.notifications]] counts what is waiting for you.
On a narrow screen the menu becomes a drawer: open it with the menu button at the top. On a wide screen [[common.menu.collapse]] at the foot of the menu leaves only its icons.

sections.heading: Sign out
steps: Open [[common.shell.account]], the round button with your initials in the top bar.
Choose [[common.signOut]].
sections.note: A session lasts a set time. When it ends, the platform asks you to sign in again. You are then taken back to the page you were on.

portfolio-dashboard.title: Your landing page: the Portfolio Dashboard
portfolio-dashboard.summary: Read the portfolio at a glance: lifecycle, health, schedule, risks, KPIs and financial position across the projects you may see.

sections.heading: What you see
paragraphs: [[common.menu.home]] opens the Portfolio Dashboard. Its heading names it for your role: [[dashboards.landing.R02]], [[dashboards.landing.R03]], [[dashboards.landing.R06]] or [[dashboards.landing.R07]]. It is one dashboard shown within your scope: a Sector Manager sees the projects of their sectors, other roles the projects their roles reach.

It shows projects by lifecycle state, Published and Current Overall Project Health, current schedule health, reporting completeness, open risks by rating, KPI condition, and the published and current financial position.

sections.heading: Read a widget correctly
paragraphs: Each widget carries a badge saying what kind of figure it is. [[dashboards.semanticState.CURRENT_LIVE]] is the latest working figure and can still change. [[dashboards.semanticState.PUBLISHED_OFFICIAL]] is what AHDA has reviewed and published. [[dashboards.semanticState.HISTORICAL_SNAPSHOT]] is a figure as it stood on an earlier date.
The foot of a widget gives its as-of date and the module that owns the figure. A total also says how many projects it counts, for example "8 of 10 projects counted", and why the others were left out.

[[dashboards.unknown.MISSING.label]] means the source has no value yet: it is not zero. [[dashboards.unknown.RESTRICTED.label]] means your role may not see that figure. [[dashboards.freshness.STALE]] means a later report is still outstanding, so the value is shown as it stood on its as-of date.

sections.heading: Narrow it down
paragraphs: If your roles give you more than one dashboard, [[dashboards.home.switch]] above the dashboard switches between them; your landing page is marked. Within a dashboard:
steps: Choose a sector in [[dashboards.filter.department]]. Only the sectors of your own projects are offered.
Choose [[dashboards.actions.refresh]] to read the figures again.
Choose [[dashboards.widget.open]] on a widget to go to the screen behind it, such as the risk register.

sections.heading: Arrange it your way
paragraphs: Portfolio Managers, Sector Managers and Executives can choose [[dashboards.personalize.open]] to hide, show and reorder the optional widgets, then [[dashboards.personalize.save]]. [[dashboards.personalize.reset]] puts the standard layout back. The fixed widgets always stay.
sections.note: Changing the layout never changes the figures, and other people keep their own layout.

sections.heading: Go further
paragraphs: The [[common.menu.portfolio]] menu also holds [[common.menu.portfolioReports]] for the detailed listings, and the [[financialKpi.nav.register]].

administrator-home.title: Your landing page as a System Administrator
administrator-home.summary: The [[dashboards.landing.R01]] and the administration screens: users, roles, organisation, integrations and audit.

sections.heading: What you see
paragraphs: [[common.menu.home]] opens the Governance Dashboard under the heading [[dashboards.landing.R01]]. It shows reporting completeness, projects by lifecycle state, open risks and their reviews, KPI condition, and the dashboard configuration backlog: where the dashboard definitions you administer stand in their lifecycle.
sections.note: Signing in as a System Administrator always needs the verification code from your authenticator app. Some administration actions ask you to confirm it again before they are carried out.

sections.heading: Administer access and organisation
paragraphs: [[common.menu.administration]] holds [[identityAccess.nav.users]], [[identityAccess.nav.roles]], [[identityAccess.nav.permissionMatrix]], [[identityAccess.nav.roleAssignments]], [[identityAccess.nav.organization]], [[identityAccess.nav.departments]] and [[identityAccess.nav.entities]].
steps: Open [[common.menu.administration]] and choose [[identityAccess.nav.users]].
Find the person and open their record.
Give or remove access through [[identityAccess.nav.roleAssignments]]: a role always applies within a scope, such as a sector or an external entity.

sections.heading: Watch integrations and the audit trail
paragraphs: [[integrationAdmin.nav.label]] shows the state of the directory, e-mail and other connected systems, with their logs. [[auditActivity.nav.label]] holds the formal [[auditActivity.nav.auditTrail]], which nobody can edit.

sections.heading: What the role does not do
paragraphs: System Administrator is not a business super-user. It administers access and configuration; it does not approve, edit or publish project data, and project screens show you only what your other roles allow.

project-manager-home.title: Your landing page as a Project Manager
project-manager-home.summary: The [[dashboards.landing.R04]]: what your projects owe, your tasks, and where to report.

sections.heading: What you see
paragraphs: [[common.menu.home]] opens the Governance Dashboard under the heading [[dashboards.landing.R04]]. Start with reporting completeness: it shows which of your projects have a progress report outstanding. Open risks and their reviews shows risks whose review is due, and KPI condition the state of your projects' indicators.

sections.heading: Work through your tasks
paragraphs: [[common.menu.myWork]] gathers [[tasks.nav.mine]], [[tasks.nav.team]], [[tasks.nav.overdue]] and [[tasks.nav.updates]], with the [[milestones.nav.register]].
steps: Open [[tasks.nav.mine]] and choose a task.
Under [[tasks.detail.work]], choose [[tasks.commands.start]], [[tasks.commands.block]], [[tasks.commands.unblock]] or [[tasks.commands.complete]] as the work moves on.
To record how far it has got, choose [[tasks.commands.reportProgress]], enter [[tasks.progress.percent]] and choose [[tasks.progress.confirm]].
sections.note: Tasks can be worked on only while the project is [[projects.status.ACTIVE]]. A blocked task must be unblocked before it can be completed, and progress is entered on a task without subtasks.

sections.heading: Your projects
paragraphs: [[projects.nav.mine]] under [[common.menu.projects]] lists the projects you manage. Opening one shows its workspace, with [[projects.workspace.tabs.overview]] first and a tab for each area: [[projects.workspace.tabs.progress]], [[projects.workspace.tabs.schedule]], [[projects.workspace.tabs.tasks]], [[projects.workspace.tabs.risks]] and more.
To report progress, see the guide on submitting a progress update.

liaison-home.title: Your landing page as a Liaison Officer
liaison-home.summary: The [[dashboards.landing.R05]]: the decisions, tasks and notifications waiting for you.

sections.heading: What you see
paragraphs: [[common.menu.home]] opens the Governance Dashboard under the heading [[dashboards.landing.R05]]. It shows the obligations that need following up across the projects you may see: reporting completeness, open risks and their reviews, and KPI condition.

sections.heading: Act on what is waiting
steps: Check the number next to [[common.menu.requestsApprovals]]: it counts the requests awaiting your decision.
Open [[approvals.nav.inbox]] and decide each request, earliest due first.
Open [[tasks.nav.mine]] under [[common.menu.myWork]] for the tasks assigned to you.
Open [[common.menu.notifications]] for alerts and escalations about the items you follow.

sections.heading: Keep track
paragraphs: [[approvals.nav.requests]] shows the requests you raised and where each one stands. [[notifications.nav.history]] shows every message the platform sent you and through which channel.

external-contributor-home.title: Your landing page as an external entity user
external-contributor-home.summary: The [[dashboards.landing.R08]]: your entity's projects, AHDA's update requests and your responses.

sections.heading: What you see
paragraphs: [[common.menu.home]] lists [[dashboards.projectLanding.caption]]: the projects shared with your entity. Open a project to see its dashboard in [[projects.workspace.tabs.overview]]: health, progress and schedule health as AHDA published them, read only and within your entity's scope.

sections.heading: Answer an update request
steps: Open [[externalParticipation.nav.mine]] under [[common.menu.requestsApprovals]].
Open the request. Its due date is marked [[externalParticipation.dueCondition.NOT_DUE]], [[externalParticipation.dueCondition.DUE]] or [[externalParticipation.dueCondition.OVERDUE]].
In [[externalParticipation.response.title]], fill in the fields AHDA asked for. Choose [[externalParticipation.actions.saveDraft]] at any time to keep your work.
When the response is complete, choose [[externalParticipation.actions.submitResponse]].
sections.note: Once submitted, a response cannot be changed. AHDA reviews it and may return it for correction.

sections.heading: Follow up your responses
paragraphs: [[externalParticipation.nav.contributions]] has two parts: [[externalParticipation.contributions.awaitingTitle]] lists the requests you have not started yet, and [[externalParticipation.contributions.historyTitle]] lists every response you have sent, with its outcome and, where AHDA returned or rejected it, AHDA's reason.
When AHDA returns a response, a new draft is opened for you with your previous values and AHDA's reason above the form. Correct it and submit it again.

register-a-project.title: Register a project
register-a-project.summary: Create a project as a draft, complete it, and submit it to AHDA for review.

sections.heading: Create the draft
paragraphs: A new project starts as a draft. It gets its [[projects.fields.formalProjectId]] only when AHDA approves it; until then the register shows it as not issued yet.
steps: Choose [[projects.nav.create]] under [[common.menu.projects]], or [[common.shell.create]] in the top bar.

Fill in [[projects.fields.title]], [[projects.fields.classification]], [[projects.fields.governanceProfile]], [[projects.fields.participation]] and [[projects.fields.department]]. For a project managed by an external entity, choose the entity as well.
Choose [[projects.create.submit]]. The project's workspace opens with the project in [[projects.status.DRAFT]].

sections.heading: Complete it
paragraphs: Choose [[projects.actions.edit]] to add the rest. Before you can submit, the project needs [[projects.fields.registrationBudget]], [[projects.fields.plannedStartDate]] and [[projects.fields.plannedEndDate]]; the governance profile you chose may require more fields, which the form marks as needed before submitting.

sections.heading: Submit it for review
steps: Choose [[projects.actions.submit]].
Name the Project Manager: yourself or someone else.
Confirm. The project becomes [[projects.status.SUBMITTED]] and goes to AHDA.
sections.note: You can withdraw a submission through [[projects.actions.changeStatus]] until AHDA starts its review.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: AHDA's review moves the project to [[projects.status.UNDER_REVIEW]]. It ends either [[projects.status.APPROVED_PLANNED]], when the Formal Project ID is issued, or [[projects.status.RETURNED]]. A returned project can be edited and submitted again as its next revision. [[projects.workspace.tabs.overview]] always says what the next step is.

submit-a-progress-update.title: Submit a progress update
submit-a-progress-update.summary: Report a project's progress to AHDA and follow it until it is published.

sections.heading: Before you start
paragraphs: Only the project's Project Manager reports progress, and only while the project is [[projects.status.ACTIVE]]. Open the project from [[projects.nav.mine]] and choose the [[projects.workspace.tabs.progress]] tab.

sections.heading: Prepare and submit the update
steps: Choose [[progress.actions.start]].
Check the planned and actual figures. They are calculated from the schedule and tasks and cannot be typed.
Keep [[progress.update.useCalculated]], or choose [[progress.update.useOverride]] and give [[progress.update.overrideReason]].
Add a [[progress.update.narrative]] explaining what changed, if you wish.
Choose [[progress.update.confirmSave]] to finish later, or [[progress.update.confirmSubmit]] when it is ready.

sections.heading: Review and publication
paragraphs: An AHDA reviewer either publishes the update or returns it with a reason. A returned update can be corrected and submitted again. The person who submitted an update can never review it.
The tab shows [[progress.official.title]], the last published figures, beside [[progress.live.title]], the latest working figures. Both show [[progress.figures.overallHealth]].
sections.note: Overall project health is calculated by the platform, not entered: it is [[progress.health.GREEN]], [[progress.health.AMBER]], [[progress.health.RED]] or, when it cannot be worked out, [[progress.health.UNKNOWN]].

decide-an-approval.title: Decide an approval
decide-an-approval.summary: Approve, return or reject the requests waiting for you, and follow the ones you raised.

sections.heading: Find what is waiting
paragraphs: [[approvals.nav.inbox]] under [[common.menu.requestsApprovals]] lists the requests waiting for your decision, earliest due first. It lists only requests within your own approval authority or authority delegated to you; a row acting for someone else says on whose behalf.

sections.heading: Make the decision
steps: Open the request and read it. [[approvals.viewHistory]] shows what happened to it before.
Choose [[approvals.decision.approve.action]], [[approvals.decision.return.action]] or [[approvals.decision.reject.action]].
Give your reason. It is required to return or reject, optional to approve, and the requester reads it.
Confirm.
sections.note: Rejecting ends the request for good. Returning ends this round and sends the request back to its author, who can correct it and submit a new revision.

sections.heading: Requests you raised
paragraphs: [[approvals.nav.requests]] shows each request you raised and its stage. While it is still pending you can withdraw it, and from its history you can escalate a decision that is overdue.
[[approvals.nav.delegations]] has two parts: [[approvals.delegations.given]] and [[approvals.delegations.received]]. A delegate can decide only what the person who delegated could decide.
